note.saw: A blank canvas and a brief: a discus, drawn in a super geometric style, inside a round badge.
note.changing: The first full render: the disc body becomes a 24-fold mandala of eye petals, string-art stars, jewels and a glowing core, crossed by nine vertical bars, with a fan tail and a spiral tunnel of tiny interlocking Escher fish behind it.
note.why: One circle inside another lets the fish and the mandala be the same thing.
note.idea: The discus has a round body and the badge is round, so the fish's body could become the central mandala of the whole badge, with a tunnel of interlocking little fish spiralling in behind it.

note.saw: The bars vanished inside the mandala, the fins were a muddy maroon, a pale fin sat on the core like a glass shard, and the background colours looked like confetti.
note.changing: Stronger bars, brighter magenta and violet fins with eyes, a rainbow spiral running through the tiles, light beams, a luminous star core, and a ring of isometric cubes and runes around the fish.
note.why: At small size the bars are what says "discus", so they had to win.

note.saw: The letter band looked sparse, with dark gaps between the small cubes, and the tail was plain next to the busy body.
note.changing: Sixty glowing three-shade cubes, hatching in the band, rainbow jewel medallions with eyes at each end of the name plate, chevrons and eyes on the tail, spikes between the body petals and bigger letters.
note.why: Every area of a DMT piece should be alive.

note.saw: The tail chevrons read as arrows fighting the fan, and the tunnel was equally bright everywhere, with no light at its centre.
note.changing: The tail is rebuilt as a jewelled rainbow fan of checkerboard cells, the pelvic fins become a slender pair, a fine lattice fills the panel behind the name, and a luminous halo glows behind the disc.
note.why: A hyperspace tunnel needs light at its end.

note.saw: One of the bars cut straight through the core eye, and the edges of the band were plain thin lines.
note.changing: The core eye moves on top of the bars on its own jewelled disc, rainbow contour echoes line both edges of the band, and a gold and magenta string-art veil spreads over the tunnel.
note.why: The third eye must never be covered.

note.saw: The paired pelvic fins read as chopsticks at badge size, and the tunnel had no sparkle.
note.changing: One swept, rayed pelvic fin replaces the pair, 32 gold rays radiate around the eye, bead rows run along the fin edges and about 70 four-point sparkles glint in the tunnel.
note.why: A fin should look like a fin even at badge size.

note.saw: The fish was darker than its surroundings: dark teal petals and heavy bars made the hero dimmer than the background.
note.changing: Brighter turquoise-to-mint petals, deep violet behind the string art instead of navy, lighter bars so the mandala glows through, and glowing ring lines in the band.
note.why: The hero has to glow more than the background.

note.saw: SavesFish said the name was not legible: thin hollow pink capitals crammed against the rim. A trial of the new name plate then showed the pelvic fin tip touching it.
note.changing: The hollow capitals give way to a bold cream SavesFish with a thick dark outline on a calm dark cartouche, well clear of the rim, and the pelvic fin is shortened so its tip clears the plate.
note.why: The name has to read instantly, and nothing should touch the letters.

note.saw: With fresh eyes, the first artist's finished draft was busy but flat: every area had the same brightness, so nothing glowed and at small size it was rainbow noise. The bars sat over the mandala like a grille, and the bubbly name plate felt like a sticker from another style.
note.changing: The piece is rebuilt from scratch: a dark ground with neon linework and light pouring out from behind the fish, a body that is a chrysanthemum of six rings of eye petals, bars that work as x-ray lenses showing the same mandala in a night palette, and new chamfered capitals made only of straight lines, SAVES on top and FISH below.
note.why: In DMT visions the brightness comes from inside, so the piece needed real darks for the light to shine against. Splitting the name top and bottom gives the badge perfect mirror symmetry.
note.idea: Start again from light and dark: a luminous fish as the brightest thing on a near-black ground, its body a true DMT chrysanthemum, its bars turned into windows onto a midnight version of the same mandala, and the name split into straight-lined geometric capitals above and below.

note.saw: The body read as a grid of eyes behind bars, the pelvic fin was a straight stick, the snout bump looked like a double chin, and the FISH band had empty dark ends.
note.changing: The bars now stop at a circle so the inner chrysanthemum glows whole, the pelvic fin curves and gains rays, the head becomes a clean round face with small lips, the bands hug their words, tiny discus hieroglyphs fill the rune ring and two luminous spiral arms sweep the tunnel.
note.why: The flower in the middle is the soul of the piece, so it must never be sliced. The tiny discus glyphs repeat the fish at a third scale, the way DMT visions repeat one motif inside itself.

note.saw: The inner flower finally glows whole and the lips make the head a real discus face. But the bars still ate half the body, the glow had gone milky grey, the bands kissed the badge rim, the fins had lost their eyes and the letters looked plain next to all the jewellery.
note.changing: Thinner bars, a clear cyan glow, bands and letters pulled in from the rim, eyes back along both fins, a 48-spike sunburst crown behind the fish, eyes and a gold echo line on the tail, and each letter cut like a jewel in cream and pale gold.
note.why: Real discus bars are slim stripes, not a cage. Faceting the capitals lets the name belong to the jewel world of the piece while staying bright enough to read from across a room.

note.saw: The first faceted letters looked like a misprinted second colour sliding off the letters, with ragged notches at the stroke ends, and the spike crown showed only around the head, like a lion's mane.
note.changing: Every stroke of every capital is now split down its middle, cream on the side facing the light and pale gold on the far side, cut exactly to the letter. The crown becomes 96 fine needles of gold and cyan light, and the tunnel gains receding rings of brightness twisted with the spiral arms.
note.why: Cut-gem capitals belong in a hyperspace temple only if every facet is crisp. Thin needles read as light pouring out of the fish instead of a costume, and the rings make the tunnel feel deep.

note.saw: The needles finally read as radiance and the tunnel has depth, but overlapping facets made the letters patchy and crossbars left gold notches on the lit strokes. The lips looked like a plug, the plain eye medallions felt like filler and the pelvic fin poked through the rune ring.
note.changing: The facets now stop cleanly wherever strokes meet, so every capital is a clean two-tone gem; the lips are rounder, the pelvic fin shorter, and the four medallions become watchers, geometric alien faces with almond eyes and a jewel third eye ringed in rainbow.
note.why: DMT visions are famous for beings that watch you; four geometric entities guarding the name add that presence while keeping the perfect symmetry.

note.saw: The watchers and gem capitals work, and the badge reads as one emblem. But the tunnel was a uniform texture with no big geometry holding it, and the corners were heavy with thick black tile outlines and a dark vignette.
note.changing: A large twelve-pointed star and a twelve-sided frame in glowing gold double lines, with cyan jewels on the rim, now hold the tunnel; the fish tiles get thinner outlines, brighter neon, tiny scale dots and a soft bloom; and jewel teeth, bead rows, dotted borders and a dashed magenta inset trim the fins, body, rune ring and name bands.
note.why: Sacred geometry works at every scale at once: the big star is the large form, the fish and bands the middle, the tiles, beads and dots the micro detail. The bloom makes the tunnel walls glow as if lit from within.

note.saw: The big star gives the tunnel a skeleton and the corners breathe. But a close-up showed the rune ring painted over the tail fan, as if the fish swam behind its own halo, and the pupil of the hero eye was a flat black hole.
note.changing: The rune ring moves behind the fish so the tail and pelvic fin overlap it, and the eye becomes a portal: 12 iris blades closing like a camera diaphragm around a cyan spiral with a pinpoint star. Faceted jewels were also meant to sit where the star's lines cross, though they never actually appeared.
note.why: Depth only works if the layers are honest, and the fish is the nearest thing in the picture. The eye is the first place anyone looks, so it should pull you inward like the tunnel does.

note.saw: The portal eye is now the strongest spot in the piece, but the tail's flat checkerboard looked like pixels next to the jewelled body, the gold outline was crisp but did not shine, and the tunnel's spiral arms were too soft to see.
note.changing: Every tail cell becomes a four-facet pyramid gem, bright stones alternating with dark amethysts lit from the top left; the fish's gold outline gets a soft bloom; and the spiral arms are narrowed and brightened so they sweep around the badge.
note.why: In a crisp geometric world the light should come from one direction everywhere, which is what makes facets look like real cut stone. The brighter spiral turns the background from a pattern into motion.

note.saw: Up close the jewel teeth on the fins read as little arrowheads and the twelve rim nodes were plain cyan dots. The crossing jewels from round 16 had never appeared, because the star's lines only cross behind the fish.
note.changing: The jewels that never appeared are dropped, the rim nodes become cut octagon jewels with lit and shaded facets and a white glint, the fin teeth become rhombus gems and a row of pearls runs down the pelvic fin.
note.why: A geometric piece is judged up close: every small part should be a real cut shape, not a placeholder, so the image keeps rewarding you the closer you look.

note.saw: The cut jewels and rhombus fin gems look right up close, but in the round badge view the twelve rim jewels were sliced in half by the badge edge, which looked accidental. (No Visionary notes arrived during my rounds.)
note.changing: The {12/5} star and its dodecagon pulled in from radius 197 to 191 so every jewel sits whole inside the badge.
note.why: In a piece built on perfect geometry, a shape cut off by the frame reads as a mistake; whole jewels make the frame feel deliberate.

note.saw: The rim jewels now sit whole. The artist also found that the Visionary's first notes had arrived a few minutes earlier, with three ideas: a Circle Limit tunnel, a spinning chrysanthemum and jewels for the plain pelvic fin.
note.changing: Each ring of eye petals is turned a little further than the one outside it, so the petals spiral around the third eye in the same direction as the spiral in the hero eye's pupil. The pelvic fin's rays are beaded in alternating magenta and gold, with a tiny almond eye where it meets the body.
note.why: A chrysanthemum that spins is the classic breakthrough image, and the twist keeps it exact geometry. Leaving no flat skin on the fish keeps the whole body alive.
note.visionary: Took the Visionary's spinning chrysanthemum and jewelled pelvic fin, but turned down its Circle Limit tunnel, since shrinking the fish toward the rim would stretch about 1,600 exact copies of one fish out of shape, work against a tunnel meant to warp toward the centre, and swell the file far past its size limit.

visions.seen: The disc is a temple gate now: the gold {12/5} star finally holds the tunnel's bones, and the four watchers have clocked me from their posts. But the Escher fish out in the tunnel are all one size, a flat rainbow wallpaper, and the chrysanthemum in the belly is perfect, so it sits still when it should be spinning.
suggestions: The Escher fish tunnel, in all four corners and the gaps between the rune ring and the bands: I see it falling away into infinity, Escher's Circle Limit. The fish could be big right next to the rune ring and shrink to glittering dust at the badge rim. In SVG, lay the tile lattice out about 3x wider than now, then warp every vertex of the tile layer: p' = c + (p - c) * Rc * tanh(1.5 * r / Rc) / r, where c is the badge centre, r = |p - c| and Rc is the corner distance (about 283 in the 400 box), so the corners still fill. Why it's more DMT: the edge stops being an edge. It becomes a place where infinitely many little fish crowd in. As a bonus, the texture around the band ends turns fine and calm, which helps the name stand clear.

The jeweled chrysanthemum in the centre of the body: let it spin. Turn each ring of eye-petals a few degrees more than the ring inside it (ring i rotated by an extra i x 6 degrees, all one way), so the petals curl into spiral arms around the central eye. Turn them the same way as the new cyan spiral in the hero eye's pupil, so both eyes drain in one direction. Why it's more DMT: the breakthrough chrysanthemum never sits still. One twist turns rings into a vortex, and it stays exact geometry.

The pink pelvic fin hanging below the body, lower centre: right now it's the only flat, quiet skin on the fish. It could get the treatment the other fins got in round 15: crenellated gold and cyan jewel teeth along its edge, each ray split into alternating magenta and gold segments, and one tiny almond eye at the root where it joins the body. Keep the tip as short as round 9 left it, well clear of the FISH band. Why it's more DMT: in hyperspace every surface is alive and watching, so no blank patch should be left on the fish.
visions.keep: The split SAVES / FISH chisel-gem capitals in cream and pale gold on their calm dark bands, untouched; the badge's mirror symmetry; the whole, unsliced chrysanthemum; the needle radiance pouring out from behind the fish; the {12/5} star and its cyan node jewels; the four watchers. Also the iris-blade eye portal with its logarithmic spiral pupil and the rune ring tucked behind the tail, both already in the newest render (#96). Leave them exactly as they are.

visions.seen: The chrysanthemum has started to turn: its petals lean into the third eye's drain, and the pelvic fin has a pulse and a little eye of its own now. I watched the tunnel stay conformal and I bow to the artist's reasons. But the halo around the fish is a soft cyan fog, the one place in this crystal temple where the geometry dissolves into haze.
suggestions: The hazy cyan glow between the fish and the rune ring, thickest left of the head and under the belly: I see the fish's aura ringing out as crisp echo contours, the silhouette repeated outward like a struck bell. Five or six thin lines (about 1.5 px) that copy the whole fish outline, fins and tail included, at Fibonacci offsets of 8, 13, 21, 34 and 55 from the gold contour, so the ripples speed up as they leave. Colour them in spectral order outward (cyan, green, gold, orange, magenta) at about 0.7 opacity, clipped inside the rune ring. In SVG, each line is one mask over a flat colour rect: the fish path stroked white at width 2d + 1.5, then the same path stroked black at width 2d - 1.5. The gaps stay open, so the needle radiance still shines through. Why it's more DMT: in hyperspace an entity vibrates and its outline repeats into the space around it. Exact offset curves turn the fog into geometry the eye can trace.

The almond eyes in the scale columns on the body, above and below the chrysanthemum, plus the four watchers in their corner posts: right now each looks its own way. I see every one of them turn to the same point. Each scale-eye's pupil slides toward the chrysanthemum's third eye: pupil = eye centre + 0.3 x the eye's half-width x the unit vector toward the third eye, clamped inside the almond. The watchers' pupils turn toward the hero eye. Why it's more DMT: the moment the room notices you. A hundred eyes locking onto one point becomes a radial field of attention, a second mandala made only of gaze, and it leads every viewer's eye straight into the spinning centre.

The cyan runes on the dark ring behind the fish: today they are a row of separate glyphs. I see them as the self-transforming language the elves sing. Build each rune from strokes on a small 3x3 dot grid (say 6 to 8 possible strokes), and let rune i use the strokes set in the bits of gray(i) = i XOR (i >> 1). Each rune then differs from its neighbour by exactly one stroke, so the writing slowly morphs as you read around the ring. With a power-of-two count (64, say, around the visible arc) the last rune is one stroke away from the first, and the sentence loops forever. Keep the same cyan, size and spacing. Why it's more DMT: a glyph that changes as you read it is the hyperspace script itself, and it's pure, rule-made geometry.
visions.keep: The split SAVES / FISH chisel-gem capitals on their calm dark bands, untouched and with nothing new touching them. The newly twisted chrysanthemum and its rainbow third eye. The iris-blade portal eye. The pyramid-gem tail. The beaded pelvic fin with its tiny almond eye (Vision 1 landed, thank you). The conformal Escher tunnel and its spiral arms. The {12/5} star with its whole octagon jewels. The four watchers. The needle radiance behind the fish, which suggestion 1 must let shine through, not cover.
